scenes.heading: Multiplying and dividing terms
scenes.sub: Numbers with numbers, letters with letters
scenes.say: Adding terms needs like terms. But here's good news: when you multiply or divide terms, you can use any terms at all.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Two teams: number players shake hands, letter players stand together
scenes.breaks: when the same letter meets itself, it doesn't just stand beside itself: a × a is written as a².
scenes.say: Think of each term as a team with a number player and a letter player. When two teams multiply, the number players shake hands, so three times four is twelve. The letter players just stand together: a b. So three a times four b is twelve a b.
scenes.caption: Think of each term as a team with a number player and a letter player. When two teams multiply, the number players shake hands, so 3 × 4 = 12. The letter players just stand together: ab. So 3a × 4b = 12ab.

scenes.heading: Same letter twice
parts: a squared: a multiplied by itself
scenes.say: When the same letter is multiplied by itself, use index notation. a times a is a squared. Don't write two a, because two a means a plus a.
scenes.caption: When the same letter is multiplied by itself, use index notation. a × a = a². Don't write 2a, because 2a means a + a.

scenes.heading: Multiplying
scenes.question: Simplify 2x × 5x.
scenes.say: Simplify two x times five x. Multiply the numbers: two times five is ten. Multiply the letters: x times x is x squared. The answer is ten x squared.
scenes.caption: Simplify 2x × 5x. Multiply the numbers: 2 × 5 = 10. Multiply the letters: x × x = x². The answer is 10x².

scenes.heading: Dividing
scenes.question: Simplify 12xy ÷ 4x.
lines: Letters: x cancels, y is left
scenes.say: To divide, write it as a fraction and cancel. Twelve x y divided by four x. Twelve divided by four is three. The x on the bottom cancels the x on top, leaving y. The answer is three y.
scenes.caption: To divide, write it as a fraction and cancel. 12xy ÷ 4x. 12 ÷ 4 = 3. The x on the bottom cancels the x on top, leaving y. The answer is 3y.

scenes.heading: Tips to remember
scenes.say: Multiply the numbers, don't add them. Remember, you can multiply any terms, not just like terms. For division, write a fraction first, then cancel. And check by multiplying your answer back.
Quick recap. Multiply the numbers, then write the letters together in alphabetical order. A letter times itself is that letter squared. And divide by cancelling. Now try the practice questions!
